MATCHING & SORTING · TODDLER 4 · AGE 2

Sort Living and Nonliving

A puppy, a tree, a ball and a book — is it alive, or not?

THE SHEET — SOLVE IT RIGHT ON IT

Your activity is ready.

Pick a color, then draw the matching lines, circle the twins or sort the groups straight on the picture with your finger, a stylus or the mouse. Press Save my work when you are proud — your drawing stays here for next time, and the picture is yours to keep.

← Fly & RollPrevious activityOdd One Out →Next activity
HOW TO DO IT

Three little steps.

  1. 1

    Meet the living things

    A puppy, a cat, a tree and a flower — they grow, they eat, they move.

  2. 2

    Meet the rest

    A ball, a car, a book and an apple — they do not grow or eat.

  3. 3

    Sort them

    Draw every picture into its box.

Ask a grown-up to read the steps aloud the first time. After that, you know just what to do.

YOUR PENCIL CASE

Pick your tools.

Pencil, nine crayons, an eraser, undo, redo and clear — the tools appear right here and work on the picture. Save keeps your finished drawing and remembers it for next time.

MY PROGRESS

Save it to keep it.

This page is cleared for you the moment you save your finished drawing. Nothing counts until then — opening the page is just opening the door.

Cleared! Your drawing is saved on this device for your child, and the ribbon is on in Class 10. Come back any time — your drawing will be waiting.

SHARE THIS ACTIVITY

Pass it on.

XFacebookWhatsApp

Share buttons open in a new tab. The copy button copies this page’s address — nothing is tracked.

ON PAPER TOO

Print the worksheet.

This sheet is also a printable worksheet with its own download and print buttons: /worksheets/toddler/matching-and-sorting/sort-living-and-nonliving/.

FOR GROWN-UPS

What this page practises.

The apple is the interesting one — it grew on a tree, but on this page it is food, so it goes with the nonliving things. Let your child wonder out loud; the wondering is the science.

  • Living and nonliving
  • Sorting by concept
  • Grouping
  • Careful thinking
